description: Refactor runMergeWatch from a blocking 240-poll (4h) loop into a one-step-per-tick state machine with durable state in .cam-merge-watch.json, so the sidecar outer loop never blocks (absorbs CAM-103) and a restart resumes from persisted state.

userStories.title: Replace blocking poll loop with pure stepMergeWatch tick
userStories.description: As the sidecar maintainer, I need runMergeWatch's blocking 240-poll loop replaced by a pure stepMergeWatch(state, now, ...) that advances one tick and returns continue|terminal, throttled to ~60s via persisted lastPolledAt, so a single tick never blocks beyond one gh poll.
acceptanceCriteria: src/release/merge-watch.ts exports stepMergeWatch(state, now, pollFn, ...) returning a discriminated result of either { kind: 'continue', state } or { kind: 'terminal', outcome }; the 240-poll for-loop in runMergeWatch is removed and no longer referenced. [oracle: file-assert grep -L 'for (let poll' src/release/merge-watch.ts returns the file (loop absent) AND grep -q 'export function stepMergeWatch' src/release/merge-watch.ts]

A tick where now < lastPolledAt + pollIntervalMs does NOT call pollFn and returns continue with state unchanged except no poll; a tick at/after the interval calls pollFn exactly once and increments pollCount and sets lastPolledAt to now. [oracle: bun test test/release/merge-watch.test.ts with an injected clock and a call-count spy on pollFn]

A legacy seed state of only { prNumber, mergedBranch } (no pollCount/lastPolledAt) is accepted and treated as fresh: pollCount starts at 0 and the first tick polls immediately (no migration, no schemaVersion field). [oracle: bun test test/release/merge-watch.test.ts feeding a two-field object and asserting the first tick calls pollFn once]

processPollResult's OPEN+BLOCKED+no-failed-check keep-polling branch (merge-watch.ts ~250-274) is preserved: an OPEN/BLOCKED status with a pending (null-conclusion) rollup returns continue, never a ci-red terminal. [oracle: bun test test/release/merge-watch.test.ts asserting OPEN_BLOCKED_PENDING yields continue]

Timeout terminal is reached when pollCount exhausts maxPolls (default 240), returning { kind: 'terminal', outcome: { kind: 'timeout', polls } }. [oracle: bun test test/release/merge-watch.test.ts driving pollCount to maxPolls]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
userStories.notes: File: src/release/merge-watch.ts (runMergeWatch:301-322 holds the for-loop; processPollResult:223-275 must be preserved verbatim; MergeWatchOptions:114-151; MergeWatchOutcome:154-158; DEFAULT_MERGE_WATCH_POLL_INTERVAL_MS=60000 and DEFAULT_MERGE_WATCH_MAX_POLLS=240 at :39/:45). Extend MergeWatchState (merge-watch.ts:58-61) with optional pollCount?: number and lastPolledAt?: number so the legacy two-field seed type-checks. Clock injection: pass `now` as a number arg to stepMergeWatch (repo pattern is `clock: () => ...`; product code uses injected clock, NOT Date.now() per the workflow lint ban). stepMergeWatch must be pure: no FS, no sleep, no Date.now(); the caller owns persistence and scheduling. Keep runMergeWatch's signature working OR delete it if no caller remains (knit via check:all dead-code gate in US-003); confirm with `grep -rn runMergeWatch src`. Tests: test/release/merge-watch.test.ts already injects fakes (sleepFn, pollFn, postMergeFn, in-memory logEvent) — extend the same harness with a clock and a pollFn call-counter. Gotcha (scripts/cam/CLAUDE.md): check:all runs knip; leaving the old loop as dead-code fails the gate (handled when wiring lands).

userStories.title: Persist merge-watch state durably across ticks in .cam-merge-watch.json
userStories.description: As the sidecar maintainer, I need a durable read/write layer for .cam-merge-watch.json that carries pollCount and lastPolledAt between ticks, removes the file only on a terminal outcome, and resumes from persisted state after a sidecar restart, so crashes do not lose progress and re-reads do not double-post-merge.
acceptanceCriteria: State persists between ticks: writing { prNumber, mergedBranch, pollCount, lastPolledAt } to .cam-merge-watch.json and reading it back round-trips all four fields. [oracle: bun test test/release/merge-watch.test.ts against a real temp-dir filesystem (tmpdir + writeFileSync/readFileSync)]

The state file is removed ONLY on a terminal outcome (merged | closed-not-merged | ci-red | timeout); a non-terminal (continue) tick leaves the file present with updated pollCount/lastPolledAt. [oracle: bun test test/release/merge-watch.test.ts asserting existsSync true after a continue tick and false after a terminal tick]

Restart-resume: after the file is written with pollCount>0 and a recent lastPolledAt, a fresh read resumes from that state (the next tick respects the persisted throttle and pollCount, not a fresh 0). [oracle: bun test test/release/merge-watch.test.ts real-fs: write state, re-read, assert resumed pollCount/lastPolledAt]

A legacy two-field seed file { prNumber, mergedBranch } reads back as fresh (pollCount 0) and a malformed/non-object file is handled without throwing. [oracle: bun test test/release/merge-watch.test.ts real-fs with a two-field file and a garbage file]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
userStories.notes: File: src/release/merge-watch.ts (add durable read/write helpers near MERGE_WATCH_FILENAME:36; MergeWatchState extended in US-001). The helpers take an explicit file path (join(claudeDir, MERGE_WATCH_FILENAME)) so tests use a tmpdir; do NOT hard-code .claude/. Read helper must tolerate: missing file (no watch), malformed JSON / non-object / array (treat as no watch, best-effort), and the legacy two-field seed (return with pollCount 0). Write helper persists all four fields. This story is the durability seam consumed by US-003's wiring; keep it pure I/O (path in, no scheduling). Gotcha (memory: merge-watch consume-on-read is by-design was the OLD model): the new model is durable, removed only at terminal — do NOT preserve the eager pre-loop delete. Tests: extend test/release/merge-watch.test.ts (it already imports readFileSync/resolve).

userStories.title: Wire one-step-per-tick into the sidecar outer loop and remove eager-delete (closes CAM-103)
userStories.description: As an operator, I need the sidecar outer loop to invoke exactly one merge-watch step per idle tick (never blocking beyond a single gh poll), keep running session-health and meta-loop checks every tick even while a watch is in progress, and run post-merge exactly once per terminal=merged detection, so the loop never wedges (CAM-103) and the watch survives restarts.
acceptanceCriteria: The production merge-watch closure in sidecar.ts no longer eager-deletes the state file before processing (the unlink-before-start at sidecar.ts ~313-314 is removed); the file is removed only when stepMergeWatch returns a terminal outcome. [oracle: file-assert grep -c 'unlinkSync' on the merge-watch closure region shows the eager pre-start delete is gone (terminal-only removal remains) AND bun test test/release/merge-watch.test.ts behavioral asserts file present after a non-terminal tick]

The outer loop (src/supervisor/loop.ts ~1405) invokes one merge-watch step per idle tick and returns promptly; hasSessionFn (loop.ts ~1424) runs every idle tick even when a watch is mid-progress (a non-terminal watch tick does not skip or block the session-health check). [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/sidecar-loop.test.ts behavioral: drive several idle ticks with a non-terminal watch and assert hasSessionFn called each tick and the loop does not block]

Each tick performs at most one gh poll: a runMergeWatchFn invocation calls the injected pollFn 0 or 1 times per tick, never looping internally. [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/sidecar-loop.test.ts with a pollFn call-counter asserting <=1 call per tick]

On terminal=merged, post-merge (pull/tag/prune) and narration run exactly once per terminal detection, and the state file is removed afterward. [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/ behavioral asserting postMergeFn called exactly once and existsSync(stateFile) false after the merged tick]

CAM-103 is closed: the outer loop is not blocked by a long watch (validated behaviorally by the multi-tick non-terminal test in this story). [oracle: reviewer-judgment grounded in the multi-tick non-blocking behavioral test above]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
Full quality spine passes including knip dead-code (the removed 240-poll loop leaves no orphan). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: Files: src/commands/sidecar.ts (makeProductionMergeWatchFn:291-350 — the eager unlink-before-start is at ~313-314; the error-path unlink at ~309 may stay as best-effort for unparseable garbage; rewrite the closure to: read durable state via US-002 helper, if absent return, else call stepMergeWatch once, persist on continue, remove file on terminal, run postMergeFn inside the merged terminal branch via processPollResult which already does it). src/supervisor/loop.ts (runMergeWatchFn awaited at 1405-1407, BEFORE hasSessionFn at 1424 — keep that ordering; one step per tick means the closure itself must be non-blocking now that the loop is gone). Gotchas (carry from spec): SIDECAR_IDLE_POLL_MS=2s but effective merge-watch cadence must stay ~60s via persisted lastPolledAt throttle (else ~7200 gh calls in 4h). The supervisor lock is NOT held on idle ticks (loop.ts ~1334); rely on single-sidecar invariant (CAM-67) + idempotent post-merge — do NOT add a pid/heartbeat owner guard (spec overrode the title). Tests: test/supervisor/sidecar-loop.test.ts + test/release/merge-watch.test.ts (cases h/i already cover idle-tick invocation gating; extend with multi-tick non-blocking + per-tick <=1 poll + post-merge-once).
